theorem_obligations.intent: Establish that execAddU32 always returns some outcome (never none) on the approved well-formed lookup domain: the guard expression resolves, and if the guard evaluates true then both source operands resolve. Option none must not be interpreted as an error (PTX-ADD-SEM2-044/045/046/050); it denotes partial execution for out-of-domain states only. This obligation encodes the critic requirement (LMAP-CRIT-F2 / risk R-2) that faithfulness theorems quantify over well-formed states.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every machine state s and every add.u32 instruction i, if evaluating the complete guard expression in s succeeds (evalGuard s i.guard = some b) and, when b is true, both source operands resolve in s (evalSource s i.a = some va and evalSource s i.b = some vb), then execAddU32 s i returns some outcome (there exists o : ExecOutcome with execAddU32 s i = some o). The theorem does not assert anything about states in which a referenced guard predicate or source register is missing; for such states none is returned, which is partiality, not an error.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem execAddU32_total_on_well_formed_lookup_domain
    (s : MachineState) (i : AddU32Instruction) (b : Bool)
    (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some b)
    (hsources : b = true -> (Exists fun va => Exists fun vb =>
        evalSource s i.a = some va /
        evalSource s i.b = some vb)) :
    Exists fun (o : ExecOutcome) => execAddU32 s i = some o
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some b  (the complete guard expression resolves in s)
hsources : if b = true then both sources resolve in s: Exists va, evalSource s i.a = some va, and Exists vb, evalSource s i.b = some vb
No other preconditions are added; in particular no dynamic precondition on source values is asserted (PTX-ADD-SEM2-038).
theorem_obligations.conclusion: Exists o : ExecOutcome, execAddU32 s i = some o (execution always yields an outcome on the well-formed lookup domain; none never occurs there).
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: Design dependencies PTX-ADD-SEM2-049 (minimal state pair), PTX-ADD-SEM2-050 (two-case outcome, no error constructor), and open questions PTX-ADD-SEM2-044/045/046/055 (no invented error/UB/implementation-defined behavior). Source basis: PTX-9.3-ADD-004 (execution description), PTX-9.3-ADD-006 (d = a + b semantics). The well-formed-domain characterization is the Lean-mapping domain requirement from the mapping critic (LMAP-CRIT-F2, risk R-2).
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The hypotheses are satisfiable: the official example add.u32 %r, %r, 4 (PTX-9.3-ADD-025) is unguarded (b = true) with source a a defined register and source b an immediate, in any state defining %r. The hypotheses are also genuinely needed: the executable example with a missing source register (guard true, evalSource returns none) yields none, showing the conclusion does not hold for arbitrary states and is not built into the type. The conclusion (existence of an outcome) is not an element of the hypotheses.
strength_risks: The theorem must not be misread as totality over all states; none for out-of-domain states is partiality (LMAP-CRIT-F2, risk R-2) and must never be described as an error/trap.

The proof is by case analysis on evalGuard and evalSource; it is a domain-characterization theorem, not a deep invariant. That is appropriate; the reviewer should confirm the hypothesis shape exactly matches the approved well-formed domain and adds no unapproved precondition.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Cases on b. If b = false, unfold execAddU32; evalGuard returns some false so the result is some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s). If b = true, use hsources to split va, vb and unfold execAddU32; evalGuard returns some true, both evalSource calls return some, so the result is some (ExecOutcome.executed (updateDestination s i.d (addU32 va vb))).
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Domain quantification for all faithfulness theorems (mapping critic LMAP-CRIT-F2); complements semantics PRF-1 well-formed-domain requirement.

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish the exact arithmetic result written on execution: when the guard is true, the destination is a register r, and both sources resolve in the pre-instruction state s, the value written to r equals addU32 applied to the source values read from s. Because addU32 is defined as (a + b) mod 2^32, the written value is the mathematical sum reduced modulo 2^32. Because the source values are read from the pre-update state s (not from any post-update state), this single theorem subsumes the read-before-write aliasing behavior (official example add.u32 %r, %r, 4, d == a): when the destination aliases a source register, the written value is computed from the pre-update value of that register. This theorem covers required areas 1 (modulo-2^32 result conformance) and 8 (read-before-write aliasing).
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every state s, instruction i, register r, and U32 values va, vb: if the complete guard expression evaluates true in s, i.d is the register destination r, evalSource s i.a = some va, and evalSource s i.b = some vb, then execAddU32 s i returns the executed outcome with some post-state s', and s'.valueRegs r = some (addU32 va vb). Here addU32 va vb is (va + vb) mod 2^32 under the human-approved formalization assumption (PTX-ADD-SEM2-015); the modulo rule is NOT an NVIDIA source fact and is never attributed to NVIDIA as explicitly specified. The equality pins the source reads to the pre-instruction state s, which is exactly the read-before-write behavior: when i.a = SourceOperand.reg r (d aliases a), va is the pre-update value s.valueRegs r, and the update uses that pre-update value.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem execAddU32_result_conforms_modulo_with_read_before_write
    (s : MachineState) (i : AddU32Instruction) (r : RegId) (va vb : U32)
    (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true)
    (hd : i.d = Destination.reg r)
    (ha : evalSource s i.a = some va)
    (hb : evalSource s i.b = some vb) :
    Exists fun (s' : MachineState) =>
      execAddU32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') /
      s'.valueRegs r = some (addU32 va vb)
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true (the complete guard expression is true, including the unguarded case)
hd : i.d = Destination.reg r (the destination is the register r; the bit-bucket destination is handled by PTX-ADD-THM-005)
ha : evalSource s i.a = some va (source a resolves in the pre-instruction state s; va is the pre-update value)
hb : evalSource s i.b = some vb (source b resolves in the pre-instruction state s; vb is the pre-update value)
theorem_obligations.conclusion:
Exists s' : MachineState, execAddU32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') /
  s'.valueRegs r = some (addU32 va vb), where addU32 va vb = (va.toFin.val + vb.toFin.val) % u32Modulus, i.e. (va + vb) mod 2^32.
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: The value content is the HUMAN_APPROVED_ASSUMPTION PTX-ADD-SEM2-015 and its derived consequences PTX-ADD-SEM2-016/029 (approved at reviews/ptx-add-u32/assumptions/ptx-add-u32-overflow-assumption-v1.json). Source evidence fragments: PTX-9.3-ADD-004 ('writes the resulting value into a destination register'), PTX-9.3-ADD-006 (semantics d = a + b), PTX-9.3-ADD-025 (official aliasing example add.u32 %r, %r, 4). Read-before-write is claim PTX-ADD-SEM2-043.
human_assumption_dependencies: PTX-ADD-SEM2-015 (human-approved modulo-2^32 result rule). The equality of the written value with (va + vb) mod 2^32 depends on this assumption; it is never attributed to NVIDIA as explicitly specified.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Satisfiable hypotheses: official examples with register/immediate sources and the unguarded or @p-true guards (e.g., state with %r = 5 and instruction add.u32 %r, %r, 7, demonstrated by #eval 12). The conclusion (exact written value in terms of pre-state source reads) is not an element of the hypotheses and distinguishes read-before-write semantics from any hypothetical read-after-write semantics; it is meaningful and non-vacuous.
strength_risks: The modulo-2^32 equality must carry the human-assumption traceability and must never be classified as an NVIDIA source fact (BLOCK-1 classification rule; risk of misattribution).
The read-before-write aspect is only as strong as the pre-state reads pinning: the statement must keep va, vb defined from the pre-instruction state s, never from the post-state s'.
The theorem does not assert behavior for missing registers; those are out-of-domain (PTX-ADD-THM-001 and LMAP-CRIT-F2).
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold execAddU32; with hguard the evalGuard match selects the some true branch; with ha, hb the two evalSource matches select some va, some vb; the result is some (ExecOutcome.executed (updateDestination s i.d (addU32 va vb))). With hd : i.d = Destination.reg r, unfold updateDestination and simplify the valueRegs update function to conclude s'.valueRegs r = some (addU32 va vb). The aliasing case i.a = SourceOperand.reg r follows with ha : evalSource s (SourceOperand.reg r) = some va and evalSource unfolds to s.valueRegs r = some va, i.e., the pre-update value.
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topics PRF-7 (arithmetic result correctness) and the read-before-write aspect of PTX-ADD-SEM2-043; PRF-6 (result-domain membership) is handled as validation obligation PTX-ADD-VAL-002.

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish that when the complete guard expression evaluates false, the instruction is not executed and the machine state is unchanged: execAddU32 returns the guardFalse outcome carrying exactly the input state s. This is the guard-false frame property (semantics future topic PRF-4), grounded in the official predication clause 'Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing' (section 9.7.13.2), which is source-supported and is NOT a human assumption. Because ExecOutcome.guardFalse carries the state and the only producer of guardFalse in execAddU32 is the unchanged input state, equality of the outcome to some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s) is a full state-preservation statement.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every state s and instruction i, if evaluating the complete guard expression in s yields some false, then execAddU32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s): the outcome is the guard-false outcome carrying exactly the input state, so no machine-state component (value register file or predicate register file) changes. The theorem also entails that source operands are not read in this branch (the code returns before evaluating sources), matching the approved guard-false behavior.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem execAddU32_guard_false_preserves_state
    (s : MachineState) (i : AddU32Instruction)
    (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some false) :
    execAddU32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s)
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some false (the complete guard expression evaluates false in s)
No source-resolution hypotheses are needed: the guard-false branch does not read source operands (this is part of the conclusion, not a precondition).
theorem_obligations.conclusion: execAddU32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s); consequently the carried state equals the input state and the instruction has no state effect.
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: Source-supported via the official predication clause (PTX-9.3-ADD-SUP2-005/006/007; section 9.7.13.2 'Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing') applied through universal predication (PTX-9.3-ADD-010/011). Claims PTX-ADD-SEM2-022 (SOURCE_FACT predication clause), PTX-ADD-SEM2-023/024/031 (DERIVED_INTERPRETATION guard-false consequence). BLOCK-2 is resolved by official evidence, not by a human assumption.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Satisfiable hypotheses: any state in which the referenced guard predicate is defined to false, or @!p with p true (the executable example @p with p=false keeps r1 at 5 demonstrates the behavior). The conclusion is not an element of the hypotheses; it pins the exact outcome constructor and the unchanged carried state, which is the semantic content of 'do nothing'.
strength_risks: The guard-false behavior must be presented as a DERIVED_INTERPRETATION from the explicit predication clause for add.u32, never as an affirmative per-instruction SOURCE_FACT that the PTX add section itself states this (BLOCK-2 classification; SEM2-024).
The theorem is stated over the bounded model state pair; it does not by itself assert anything about components outside the model (see deferred property D-2).
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold execAddU32; with hguard the evalGuard match selects the some false branch, which returns some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s) directly; the source-evaluation branch is never reached. No source-resolution case analysis is needed.

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish the destination-only update / frame property for a register destination: when the instruction executes with guard true and destination register r, the only value register that may change is r; every other value register and every predicate register is unchanged. This single theorem merges required areas 3 (predicate-register preservation), 4 (unrelated-value-register frame property), and 5 (destination-only update) into one stronger frame statement. The theorem is stated over the bounded model (value-register file plus predicate-register file) and retains the documented negative-evidence caveat: the bounded model contains no carry-flag, status-register, or condition-code component, and the absence of such writes is absence-based negative evidence (SEM2-CRIT-F1 / LMAP-CRIT-F1 / risk R-1), not an affirmative NVIDIA enumeration; the frame claim must not be cited as an explicit NVIDIA statement about components outside the model.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every state s, instruction i, register r, and U32 values va, vb: if the complete guard expression evaluates true in s, i.d is the register destination r, and both sources resolve in s with values va and vb, then execAddU32 s i returns the executed outcome with some post-state s' such that (1) every value register r' different from r has the same value in s' as in s; and (2) every predicate register p has the same value in s' as in s. The theorem does not assert that the destination register itself keeps its old value (it is updated with addU32 va vb per PTX-ADD-THM-002), and it does not make any claim about carry-flag/status components outside the bounded model.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem execAddU32_destination_only_frame
    (s : MachineState) (i : AddU32Instruction) (r : RegId) (va vb : U32)
    (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true)
    (hd : i.d = Destination.reg r)
    (ha : evalSource s i.a = some va)
    (hb : evalSource s i.b = some vb) :
    Exists fun (s' : MachineState) =>
      execAddU32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') /
      (forall (r' : RegId), r' != r -> s'.valueRegs r' = s.valueRegs r') /
      (forall (p : PredId), s'.predRegs p = s.predRegs p)
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true
hd : i.d = Destination.reg r
ha : evalSource s i.a = some va
hb : evalSource s i.b = some vb
theorem_obligations.conclusion: Exists s', execAddU32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') and (forall r' != r, s'.valueRegs r' = s.valueRegs r') and (forall p, s'.predRegs p = s.predRegs p).
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: Semantics claims PTX-ADD-SEM2-007/028/029 (destination-only update; no other value register, predicate register, carry flag, or status component is proposed to be written because the source states no such write) and PTX-ADD-SEM2-049 (minimal state pair). Source evidence: PTX-9.3-ADD-004, PTX-9.3-ADD-006. The absence of carry/status writes is NEGATIVE evidence (SEM2-CRIT-F1 / LMAP-CRIT-F1; risk R-1) and the frame theorem must retain this caveat.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Satisfiable hypotheses: the executable example with r1 = 1, r2 = 2 and updateDestination (Destination.reg r1) (mkU32 100) shows r1 becomes 100 while r2 remains 2 and the predicate file is untouched. The conclusion (all other registers and all predicates preserved) is not an element of the hypotheses; it is the frame content and distinguishes destination-only semantics from any semantics writing additional state.
strength_risks: Risk R-1 (LMAP-CRIT-F1 / SEM2-CRIT-F1): the theorem must be stated over the bounded model only and must not be cited as an explicit NVIDIA statement that 'no carry flag / status register is written'. The absence-based caveat must remain traceable until final acceptance.
The theorem does not prove the value written to r (that is PTX-ADD-THM-002); a reviewer should ensure no attempt to strengthen this theorem into an assertion about components outside the model.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold execAddU32 and updateDestination with hd; the resulting state updates valueRegs via the function fun r' => if r' == r then some result else s.valueRegs r'. Use by_cases (r' == r) or simp on the DecidableEq of RegId to prove r' != r -> s'.valueRegs r' = s.valueRegs r'; predicate registers are untouched because only the valueRegs field is updated in the record (predRegs equality by record simplification).
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-2 (destination-only update / frame), with negative-evidence caveat from risk R-1.

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish the bit-bucket discard property: when the destination is the bit bucket '_', the instruction executes (guard true, sources resolve) but no value register is written and the whole state is unchanged. This covers required area 6 (bit-bucket state preservation) and corresponds to semantics future topic PRF-3. The obligation retains the documented strength caveat: the no-write consequence is supported only to the strength of the general section 9.2 bit-bucket rule (AMB-1 / PTX-ADD-SEM2-030/054 / risk R-4); the add section does not demonstrate the bit-bucket form, so the theorem must not be presented as an add-specific explicit source fact.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every state s and instruction i, if the complete guard expression evaluates true in s, i.d is the bit bucket Destination.bitBucket, and both sources resolve in s, then execAddU32 s i returns the executed outcome with some post-state s' and s' = s: the computed result is discarded and no value register or predicate register changes. The strength of this claim is limited to the general section 9.2 bit-bucket rule (PTX-ADD-SEM2-030/047); add-specific demonstration is absent (PTX-ADD-SEM2-054).
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem execAddU32_bit_bucket_preserves_state
    (s : MachineState) (i : AddU32Instruction) (va vb : U32)
    (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true)
    (hd : i.d = Destination.bitBucket)
    (ha : evalSource s i.a = some va)
    (hb : evalSource s i.b = some vb) :
    Exists fun (s' : MachineState) =>
      execAddU32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') /
      s' = s
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true
hd : i.d = Destination.bitBucket (destination is the bit bucket '_')
ha : evalSource s i.a = some va
hb : evalSource s i.b = some vb
theorem_obligations.conclusion: Exists s', execAddU32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') and s' = s (the executed outcome's state is exactly the input state; the result is discarded).
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: Semantics claims PTX-ADD-SEM2-047 (SOURCE_FACT general section 9.2 bit-bucket rule), PTX-ADD-SEM2-030 (DERIVED_INTERPRETATION no-write consequence, supported to the strength of the general rule), PTX-ADD-SEM2-054 (OPEN_QUESTION: add-specific bit-bucket demonstration absent). Evidence fragment: PTX-9.3-ADD-015.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Satisfiable hypotheses: any state in which the sources resolve and the destination is '_' (the executable example with bit bucket keeps r1 at 1 demonstrates the no-write behavior). The conclusion s' = s is not an element of the hypotheses; it is the discard content and distinguishes the bit-bucket destination from the register destination (PTX-ADD-THM-002/004).
strength_risks: Risk R-4 (AMB-1 / PTX-ADD-SEM2-054): the theorem must not be presented as add-specific explicit NVIDIA behavior; it is supported only to the strength of the general section 9.2 rule. PRF-3 strength must not exceed this.
The theorem still requires source resolution (well-formed domain); a reviewer should confirm the hypothesis set matches the guard-true read-before-write flow of the approved semantics.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold execAddU32; with hguard the evalGuard match selects the some true branch; with ha, hb both evalSource calls resolve; the result is some (ExecOutcome.executed (updateDestination s i.d (addU32 va vb))). With hd : i.d = Destination.bitBucket, unfold updateDestination: the bitBucket branch returns s, so the executed state equals s; simp.
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-3 (bit-bucket discard), with AMB-1 strength caveat.

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish the guard-behavior equivalence (semantics future topic PRF-5): on the approved well-formed lookup domain, the executed outcome occurs if and only if the complete guard expression evaluates true. This covers the no-guard, @p, and @!p cases uniformly through evalGuard and pins the outcome classification of execAddU32. It complements PTX-ADD-THM-003 (guard-false state preservation) by providing the reverse direction: an executed outcome implies the guard was true, so an instruction can never execute under a false complete guard.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every state s and instruction i, if the complete guard expression resolves in s to some b and, when b is true, both sources resolve in s, then there exists an executed outcome from execAddU32 s i if and only if b is true. Equivalently: execution happens exactly when the complete guard expression is true; when b is false the outcome is the guard-false outcome (and, by PTX-ADD-THM-003, the state is unchanged).
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem execAddU32_executes_iff_guard_true
    (s : MachineState) (i : AddU32Instruction) (b : Bool)
    (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some b)
    (hsources : b = true -> (Exists fun va => Exists fun vb =>
        evalSource s i.a = some va /
        evalSource s i.b = some vb)) :
    (Exists fun (s' : MachineState) =>
        execAddU32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')) <-> b = true
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some b

hsources : if b = true then both sources resolve in s (Exists va, Exists vb, evalSource s i.a = some va /
    evalSource s i.b = some vb)
No additional guard or source preconditions.
theorem_obligations.conclusion: (Exists s', execAddU32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')) <-> b = true.
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: Semantics claims PTX-ADD-SEM2-023 (complete guard-expression evaluation model: unguarded true, @p the predicate value, @!p the negation), PTX-ADD-SEM2-024 (false complete guard -> instruction not executed), PTX-ADD-SEM2-050 (two-case outcome design). Source evidence: PTX-9.3-ADD-010/011/016/018 and the predication clause PTX-9.3-ADD-SUP2-005/006/007.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Both directions are non-trivial. Forward: with b = true and hsources, the code reaches the executed branch (this uses source resolution). Reverse: with b = false, the code returns guardFalse, so no executed outcome exists. There exist states satisfying the hypotheses for both values of b (e.g., @p with p true and with p false), and the theorem's biconditional is false if the outcome classification were wrong, so it is not vacuous.
strength_risks: The theorem is a classification/guard-behavior statement, not a determinism claim; it must not be mistaken for PRF-1 (determinism), which is deferred (see deferred property D-1).

The hypothesis shape must match the well-formed lookup domain exactly; adding source-resolution hypotheses unconditionally (even when b = false) would be an unapproved strengthening and would make the reverse direction trivial in a different way.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold execAddU32. Forward direction: assume b = true, use hsources to split va, vb; evalGuard gives some true, both evalSource calls give some, so the result is some (ExecOutcome.executed _). Reverse direction: assume Exists s', execAddU32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s'); the evalGuard match in execAddU32 must have taken the some true branch (the some false branch returns guardFalse and the none branch returns none), hence b = true (use hguard and injectivity of some).
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-5 (guard behavior: executes iff complete guard expression true).

deferred_properties.title: Determinism of a relational execution semantics (PRF-1 / PTX-ADD-SEM2-042)
deferred_properties.description: The semantics lists determinism of the execution relation as future proof obligation PRF-1 (claim PTX-ADD-SEM2-042). In the current Lean mapping, execAddU32 is a function from (state, instruction) to Option ExecOutcome; a statement that 'the function returns one value' would be a trivial fact of function application, not a meaningful determinism theorem. Architecture design D-25 (PTX-ADD-SEM2-052) deliberately reserves a relational execution semantics so that determinism and frame obligations are non-vacuous. Until a relational semantics exists in this bounded unit, determinism is deferred and must not be stated as a functional triviality.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: Functional single-valuedness would be vacuous; relational semantics (design D-25) is not yet part of the Lean mapping.

deferred_properties.title: Whole-PTX frame claims about components outside the minimal state (carry flags, status/condition-code registers, memory, shared, special registers)
deferred_properties.description: The bounded model is the minimal approved pair (value-register file, predicate-register file). Statements such as 'add.u32 writes no carry flag or status register' are absence-based negative evidence (SEM2-CRIT-F1 / LMAP-CRIT-F1 / risk R-1), not affirmative NVIDIA enumeration. No theorem is proposed over components outside the bounded model; PTX-ADD-THM-004 is stated strictly over the model and retains the caveat.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: Requires a broader machine model outside this bounded unit; negative evidence must not be presented as an affirmative theorem.

deferred_properties.title: Add-specific bit-bucket source demonstration (PTX-ADD-SEM2-054 / AMB-1)
deferred_properties.description: PTX-ADD-THM-005 states the no-write consequence at the strength of the general section 9.2 rule (PTX-ADD-SEM2-030/047). Whether the add section itself demonstrates the bit-bucket form remains an open question (AMB-1). Strengthening the bit-bucket theorem into an explicit add-specific source claim is deferred pending official evidence.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: Open question PTX-ADD-SEM2-054; add-specific demonstration absent.

deferred_properties.title: Constant-immediate range/encoding well-formedness (PTX-ADD-SEM2-053 / AMB-4)
deferred_properties.description: The allowed range and encoding of constant immediate source operands is not stated in the evidence. This affects static well-formedness of programs only and does not change the state transition of a given legal instruction. Any theorem about which immediates are legal is deferred.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: Open question PTX-ADD-SEM2-053; static well-formedness, outside executable-semantics scope.

deferred_properties.title: Version and target gating theorems (PTX-ADD-SEM2-036/037/051)
deferred_properties.description: Base add.u32 is introduced in PTX ISA 1.0 and supported on all target architectures. These are static validation-layer obligations, not executable state-transition behavior; the Lean candidate does not model version/target metadata (mapping critic LMAP-CRIT-F5). Theorems about version/target validity are deferred to the validation layer.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: Version/target metadata is outside the executable mapping scope of the bounded unit.

deferred_properties.title: Behavior on out-of-domain states (missing guard predicate or source register)
deferred_properties.description: For states in which a referenced guard predicate or source register is not defined, execAddU32 returns none. This is PARTIAL execution for out-of-domain states, not an error, trap, undefined behavior, or implementation-defined behavior (PTX-ADD-SEM2-044/045/046/050; LMAP-CRIT-F2; risk R-2). No theorem will be stated about 'error' behavior, and none must never be interpreted as an approved error.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: The approved semantics fixes behavior only for the well-formed domain; out-of-domain behavior is a partiality convention, not a semantic property.

deferred_properties.title: Error / undefined / implementation-defined behavior claims (PTX-ADD-SEM2-044/045/046/055)
deferred_properties.description: No explicit error, trap, undefined-behavior, or implementation-defined-behavior clause for add was found in the evidence; none is invented. Whether the absence means no such behaviors exist is an open question (PTX-ADD-SEM2-055). Any future claim of such behavior requires official evidence and is deferred.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: Absence of evidence; no behavior invented; any positive claim would require new official evidence.

deferred_properties.title: Publication of the SHA-256 of the human assumption decision record (PTX-ADD-SEM2-058)
deferred_properties.description: The human-approved overflow-assumption record (reviews/ptx-add-u32/assumptions/ptx-add-u32-overflow-assumption-v1.json) does not publish its own SHA-256; no value is fabricated. A future verification pass should compute and record the decision record's own SHA-256 (traceability gap SEM2-CRIT-F2; risk R-3). This is a metadata closure item, not a theorem.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: Known traceability gap accepted at Gate B as non-blocking; requires future verification tooling.

known_risks.description: Negative-evidence caveat for the frame/no-carry statements (LMAP-CRIT-F1 / SEM2-CRIT-F1). PTX-ADD-THM-004 and any frame reasoning must be stated over the bounded model and must not cite 'no carry flag / status register is written' as an explicit NVIDIA statement. Caveat retained in PTX-ADD-THM-004 and deferred property D-2; must remain traceable until final acceptance.

Option none is partiality, not an error (LMAP-CRIT-F2). All faithfulness theorems quantify over the approved well-formed lookup domain via lookup-success hypotheses (PTX-ADD-THM-001 shape); none must never be interpreted as an approved error/trap/UB behavior.
The human assumption decision record's SHA-256 is not published (PTX-ADD-SEM2-058). Deferred property D-8; must be closed before final acceptance.
Bit-bucket strength is limited to the general section 9.2 rule (AMB-1 / PTX-ADD-SEM2-054). PTX-ADD-THM-005 retains the strength caveat and is not presented as add-specific explicit behavior.
Constant-immediate range/encoding remains open (PTX-ADD-SEM2-053). Affects static well-formedness only; deferred property D-4.

Theorem statements in this specification are Lean sketches, not compiled Lean. Independent theorem-strength review must validate each statement's hypotheses, non-vacuity, and faithfulness before any proof file is written.

human_assumption.attribution_rule: Modulo-2^32 behavior is never classified SOURCE_FACT and is never attributed to NVIDIA as explicitly specified; only PTX-ADD-THM-002 depends on it.

traceability_summary.determinism_note: PRF-1 determinism over a relation is deferred (PTX-ADD-DEF-001): the mapping provides a function execAddU32, so a functional single-valuedness statement would be vacuous; relational semantics is future design D-25.
